name: Hydrogen
role: SEI reduction and impurity chemistry. LiH is a hydride SEI reduction product (recently argued beneficial); LiOH is a moisture/hydroxyl SEI phase; residual protons/H2O are a contaminant axis that attacks sulfide SE (H2S) and Li metal.
ionic_radius_note: Hydride H- radius is large and host-dependent (~1.3-1.5 A; in LiH, a=4.08 A rock salt gives ~1.3 A). H+ is a bare proton with no meaningful ionic radius (effectively a point charge). Approximate.

representative_compounds.battery_role: hydride SEI from reduction of trace H (solvent/moisture) at Li metal; recently identified as stabilizing rather than purely detrimental; extremely air-sensitive
representative_compounds.note: rock-salt (Fm-3m), wide-gap ionic insulator (exp gap ~5 eV). XPS-hard: Li 1s overlaps Li metal/Li2O and H has no core level -> best identified by cryo-ToF-SIMS. First-order Raman inactive (centrosymmetric); monitored via corrosion products (LiOH/Li2CO3).

representative_compounds.battery_role: hydroxyl SEI from moisture; ionically resistive; converts to Li2CO3 on CO2 exposure
representative_compounds.note: O 1s ~531 eV; O-H Raman stretch ~3676 cm-1.

representative_compounds.battery_role: moisture -> LiOH/LiH/H2 at Li metal; with sulfide SE -> H2S evolution and SE degradation; dryness control axis
representative_compounds.note: not a phase to engineer but to exclude; central to sulfide-SSB handling.

sei_relevance: LiH forms by reduction of trace hydrogen (from solvent/moisture) at Li metal; long considered a detrimental dead-Li-like phase, recent work argues it can stabilize the anode. It is one of the hardest SEI species to detect: extremely air-sensitive and easily mis-assigned as Li metal or Li2O in XPS, so cryo-ToF-SIMS is the reliable probe. LiOH (moisture-derived) is resistive and converts to Li2CO3. Hydrogen is largely an impurity/control axis: in sulfide SSBs, moisture drives H2S evolution and LiOH formation, so low H is a processing requirement rather than an engineered interphase.

xps.assignment: LiH - NOT a clean isolated peak; overlaps Li metal (~52-53), Li2O and LiF (~55-56). Inferred, not resolved
xps.ref: XPS SEI primer, ACS Energy Lett. 2022; cross-check by ToF-SIMS
battery-interphase IR/Raman/XPS database arXiv:2310.13871; SEI XPS reviews

xps_note: Hydrogen itself is XPS-invisible: its only electron (H 1s) is a valence electron, so H-bearing SEI phases are identified through the partner element (Li 1s for LiH, O 1s for LiOH) plus ToF-SIMS/Raman, never a direct H core line.

raman.assignment: LiOH O-H stretching mode (hydroxyl SEI marker)

raman_note: LiH has no first-order Raman signal (rock-salt, centrosymmetric Oh); its presence is tracked spectroscopically via corrosion products (LiOH/Li2CO3) - see LiH-corrosion Raman study (OSTI).
dos_character: LiH is an ionic wide-gap insulator (rock-salt): a filled H- (H 1s-derived) valence band and empty Li 2s conduction band, experimental gap ~5 eV (DFT/PBE underestimates). LiOH is likewise a wide-gap insulator (layered), valence band O 2p/OH. Both are strongly electron-insulating (good passivation) but only modest Li+ conductors, so hydride/hydroxyl-rich SEI tends to be resistive.
key_references: Identifying the positive role of lithium hydride in stabilizing Li-metal anodes 2022 (PMC8782449) - LiH as beneficial SEI
Cryogenic ToF-SIMS for air-sensitive LiH in Li-metal anodes 2024/2025, Microsc. Microanal. - detection strategy where XPS fails
An XPS Primer for SEI Characterization in Li-Metal Anodes 2022, ACS Energy Lett. - LiH/inorganic SEI XPS caveats
Battery-interphase IR/Raman/XPS database 2023, arXiv:2310.13871 - LiOH/Li2CO3 fingerprints (O 1s ~531 eV, OH ~3676 cm-1)
Raman Spectroscopy of Lithium Hydride Corrosion (OSTI 1018047) - LiH -> LiOH/Li2CO3 corrosion tracking
